extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, patent attorneys, and pleaders preparing or defending patent infringement actions (U.S. jurisdiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for drafting declarations/pleadings and for pleading defenses in U.S. patent infringement actions, including required allegations, notice/marking rules, special pleading forms, and the full enumeration of defeasible grounds. Emphasizes what must be alleged, how notices/pleas should be made, and procedural timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allege ownership during infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: The plaintiff must allege that he became the owner of the patent right, and must also allege ownership during the time of the infringement upon which the declaration is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title papers should be set forth by their legal effect and not copied bodily into the declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profert of title papers (when required)
rubrics_metrics.description: No profert need be made in any declaration of any assignment or grant of any interest under letters patent; but where title papers include letters testamentary or letters of administration, the plaintiff must make profert of those documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If profert is made of any document not necessary, it will be treated as surplusage and will not entitle the defendant to oyer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking / notice allegation ( §433a )
rubrics_metrics.description: The declaration must state either that no person ever made or sold the patented article under the authority of the patent; or that those made/sold had the word 'patented' with the day and year the patent was granted fixed thereon (or on the package); or that the defendant was duly notified of the infringement and continued to infringe after such notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides alternative ways to plead notice/marking; failure to mark or notify may be raised as a defense (see failure-to-mark defense).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of infringement content
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of infringement should allege that the defendant, without any license, did make, or did use, or did sell, the subject of whatever claim or claims the plaintiff intends to prosecute at the trial; and that the infringement occurred within the territory covered by the plaintiff's title and within the time the plaintiff held title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While alleging any one of making, using, or selling is sufficient to show a cause of action, evidence of one will not support proof of another; therefore plead as many types (make/use/sell) as the plaintiff expects to be able to prove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of time of infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: The time of the infringement is properly stated by alleging it occurred on a specified day and on divers other days between that day and some later specified date; plaintiff will not be permitted to prove infringement outside the time specified in the declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to plead the six-year statutory period; lack of infringements within the statutory period is a defense and need not be specially pleaded by the defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated infringements and title timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated infringements may be sued for in one action, but all infringements complained of in one declaration must have been committed after the plaintiff obtained title to the patent and before the beginning of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If plaintiff is an assignee who also purchased earlier rights, a separate action (in the name of the prior owner) is required for infringements accruing before the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special statement of damages required
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages incurred by the plaintiff on account of a defendant's infringement must be stated specially, because no particular damage is necessarily implied by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The particular special damages depend upon the criterion of damages relied upon (established royalty, loss or reduction of sales, reduction of prices, etc.); the pleader should select the measures of damages he expects to prove and draw his special statement accordingly so the defendant is apprised of issues to prepare for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion—allege right to actual and treble damages
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusion of a proper declaration alleges that, by force of the statutes of the United States, a right of action has accrued to recover the actual damages specified and such additional amount, not exceeding in the whole three times the amount of such actual damages, as the court may adjudge, besides costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conclusion also ends with the ancient allegation of bringing suit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of declaration—substance over form
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration, though not drawn in due form, is sufficient if it contains all that is essential to enable the plaintiff to give evidence of his right and of its violation and affords to the defendant the opportunity of interposing every defence allowed by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts do not encourage merely technical objections to pleadings and will seek to sustain pleadings that are substantially sufficient for the real purposes of pleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilatory pleas follow common-law rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Dilatory pleas in patent actions are not materially different from corresponding pleas in other common-law cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent pleaders may refer to standard works on common-law pleading for preliminary defenses; no special treatment is necessary in this treatise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 1: matter not statutory subject of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: That the matter covered by the letters patent was not a statutory subject of a patent (e.g., a principle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defence is mainly applicable when a 'principle' has been patented; judicial notice is often available for this defence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 2: not an invention
rubrics_metrics.description: That it was not an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defence may sometimes be amenable to judicial notice, but generally requires evidence if based on facts outside the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 3: not novel (want of novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: That it was not novel at the time of its alleged invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defence may be made under the general issue accompanied by statutory notice or by special plea; notices of want of novelty must state names and dates of prior patentees, and where prior knowledge/use is relied upon must state names and residences of persons and locations (cities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 4: not useful (lack of utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: That it was not useful at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not among those defenses suitable for the general issue with notice and usually requires a special plea with evidentiary support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 5: inventor actually abandoned the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: That the inventor actually abandoned the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be pleaded under the general issue accompanied by statutory notice or by special plea; requires evidence outside the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 6: constructive abandonment (failure to apply in time)
rubrics_metrics.description: That he constructively abandoned it by not applying for a patent during the time allowed by the statutes for application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be made under the general issue with notice or by special plea; requires evidence outside the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 7: claims differ from original application (lack of original support)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the invention claimed in the original patent is substantially different from any indicated, suggested, or described in the original application therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational on the spirit of patent laws; evidence must be drawn from outside the patent and introduced regularly; normally made by special plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 8: patentee surreptitiously or unjustly obtained patent (prior conceiver)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patentee surreptitiously or unjustly obtained the patent for that which was in fact the invention of another who was using reasonable diligence in adapting and perfecting the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be made under general issue with notice or by special plea; where pleaded, all elements (including prior conceiver's reasonable diligence) must be incorporated in the plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 9: made by another jointly with sole applicant (inventorship dispute)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the invention was made by another jointly with the sole applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cannot be supported from the face of the patent; depends on extrinsic evidence and must be interposed by special plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 10: made by one only of two or more joint applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: That it was made by one only of two or more joint applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly depends on evidence aliunde and must be pleaded specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 11: specification made to cover less/more than whole truth (fraudulent description)
rubrics_metrics.description: That for the purpose of deceiving the public, the description and specification filed in the Patent Office was made to cover less than the whole truth relevant to the invention, or was made to cover more than was necessary to produce the desired effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be set up under the general issue with statutory notice or by special plea; this defence must be stated with particularity and requires proof of intent to deceive (although intent may be implied from knowledge of importance of omitted/inserted matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 12: insufficient specification / failure to enable ( § statutory enablement )
rubrics_metrics.description: That the description of the invention in the specification is not in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art to make, construct, compound, and use the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defence cannot be based on the general issue with notice, and whether a patent falls below the statutory requirement is a question of evidence (not mere construction); it cannot be established by demurrer and must be interposed in a special plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 13: claims not distinct (nebulous claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the claims of the patent are not distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at nebulous claims; may be made by demurrer because it is often a question of construction of the document, though a special plea is often the best means of interposing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 14: unreasonable delay to enter a needed disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patentee unreasonably delayed to enter a needed disclaimer where both new and old inventions are claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether delay is unreasonable is a question of fact depending on evidence and generally requires a special plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 15: original surrendered and reissued without statutory foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: That the original patent was surrendered and reissued in the absence of every statutory foundation therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goes to the jurisdiction of the Commissioner to reissue; questions are mainly factual and discussed in chapter on reissues—best raised by special plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 16: reissue claims broader than original and delayed application
rubrics_metrics.description: That the claims of the reissue patent in suit are broader than those of the original, and that the reissue was not applied for until a long time had elapsed after the original was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First element requires comparative construction of original and reissue; second element (delay) is a variable fact depending on circumstances—both elements are factual and should be pleaded by special plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 17: reissue covers different invention from original
rubrics_metrics.description: That the reissue patent in suit covers a different invention from any which the original patent shows was intended to be secured thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depends on proof of the original patent and may require complicated evidence; typically raised by special plea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 18: claimed invention identical to prior patent by same inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: That the invention claimed in the original patent is substantially identical with an invention claimed in a prior patent granted on the application of the same inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assails validity of original patents; may be applicable to all or some claims and will invalidate only the claims that are shown to be invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 19: patent repealed
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patent was repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When true, will be a full defence to any action based on alleged infringements committed after the repeal; effect on infringements before repeal depends on whether repeal is ab initio or in futuro.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 20: patent legally expired before alleged infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patent legally expired before the alleged infringement began or before it ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: where foreign patent expired before U.S. patent purported termination; this defence, if successful, limits duration but does not affect patent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 21: failure to mark / notify (unmarked specimens and no notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patentee made or sold specimens of the invention without marking them 'patented' and without notifying the defendant of his infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If successful, will bar the action as to unnotified infringements, but will not affect patent validity; oral or written notice that was given and did not stop infringement will oust the defence as to subsequent infringements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 22: plaintiff lacks title to the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: That the plaintiff has no title to the patent, or no such title as can enable him to maintain the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A plea in bar that may be partial or total depending on title facts; must be pleaded appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 23: defendant has license
rubrics_metrics.description: That the defendant has a license which authorized part or all of the doings which constitute the alleged infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be pleaded as a defence to liability; requires evidentiary support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 24: defendant has release
rubrics_metrics.description: That the defendant has a release, discharging him from liability on account of part or all of the alleged infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A release is a bar to the extent it covers the alleged acts and must be pleaded and proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 25: non-infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: That the defendant is not guilty of any infringement of the patent upon which he is sued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic defense of non-infringement and is often pleaded as the general issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 26: estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: That the plaintiff is estopped from enforcing any right of action against the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable/arguable bar based on plaintiff's conduct; may be partial or total and requires factual proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 27: statute of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: That the cause of action sued upon is partly or wholly barred by some statute of limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute of limitation is a defense of timing; may be availabe without special plea in some circumstances but is generally pleaded; defendant need not specially plead restriction in some contexts because facts may appear in plaintiff's case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense 28: Commissioner exceeded authority in granting/reissuing
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Commissioner of Patents has exceeded his legal authority in granting or reissuing the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defense assails the administrative grant/reissue and is discussed in reissue chapters; may be raised by demurrer or plea depending on whether question is one of construction or of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which defenses attack patent validity versus personal/bar defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The first fourteen and the twenty-eighth defenses assail the validity of original patents; fifteenth–seventeenth assail reissues; defenses twenty-one through twenty-seven are without relevancy to validity and concern personal/bar matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful validity defenses will defeat the patent and actions based thereon; defenses that are personal (e.g., license, release, marking, limitations) may bar the action without affecting patent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demurrer vs plea—when defenses are amenable to demurrer
rubrics_metrics.description: Defenses which can be established from the face of the declaration, the letters patent, or facts of which the court will take judicial notice may be made by demurrer; otherwise they must be pleaded specially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defense is made by demurrer and overruled, it cannot later be made in a plea without leave of court.

rubrics_metrics.name: General issue accompanied by statutory notice (which defenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent statute provides that five defenses (those numbered 3, 5, 6, 8, and 11 in Section 440) may be made under the general issue, accompanied with a certain statutory notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either of these five defenses may also be made under a special plea instead; if defendant uses both forms for the same defense, court will require him to elect one. Notices must be in writing and served at least thirty days before trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of special matter—form, timing, and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of special matter must be in writing and served on the plaintiff or his attorney at least thirty days before trial; they need not be filed in court and their sufficiency is decided at trial by admitting or excluding evidence offered thereunder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of want of novelty must state names and dates of prior patentees; notices relying on prior knowledge/use must state names and residences and city of occurrence; prior printed publications must be identified with sufficient definiteness to permit locating the passages relied upon. Notices need not state the precise time of publication/use (except dates for patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions and notices of special matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositions taken before service of the statutory notice are as admissible under it as if taken afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute's purpose is to give plaintiff thirty days before trial to secure evidence to contradict defendant's witnesses; it does not obligate defendant to give notice before taking depositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial notice and defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any defence can be based upon a fact of which the court will take judicial notice without evidence, that defence may be made under the general issue without any special pleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first and second defenses are mainly within the rule of judicial notice (e.g., 'principle' patents); but when want of invention is based on facts outside the patent, it must still be pleaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special plea timing and effect of striking
rubrics_metrics.description: Special pleas (when used instead of notices) must be filed at least thirty days before the term of trial or the plaintiff will be entitled to a continuance; a special plea stricken out by order of court does not operate as a notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have inherent power to regulate filing times; failure to timely file special plea may result in continuance for plaintiff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirement for many defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Many defenses (notably those attacking inventorship, abandonment, novelty by prior use, surreptitious obtaining, reissue scope/validity, etc.) require evidence outside the patent and cannot be disposed of by mere record inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such defenses should be pleaded by special plea so the plaintiff is notified and can prepare evidence to meet them.
